title: Passwords as an optional fallback
description: Keep passwords for people who cannot create a passkey, but make them a deliberate, better-protected option. A user may add or remove a password from their 'Sign-in methods' page (never removing their last method). Add a policy: minimum length 12, rejection of a short list of common passwords, no composition rules. Add self-service password change requiring the current password or a fresh passkey assertion. Add an instance setting 'Require passkeys for administrators'. Standardise hashing cost in one place and rehash on next sign-in where an older cost is found.

recommended_model.name: Opus 5.5
recommended_model.rationale: Several interacting rules (last-method guard, admin requirement) but a clear specification.

acceptance_criteria: A user with a passkey can add or remove a password; a user with only a password is prompted (never forced, unless the admin setting applies) to add a passkey
New and changed passwords must be at least 12 characters and not on the common-password list
Changing a password requires re-authentication and ends the user's other sessions
With 'Require passkeys for administrators' on, admin-role accounts cannot sign in by password, and the setting cannot be enabled until every administrator has a passkey
Hash cost is a single constant; older hashes are upgraded transparently at sign-in
testing_requirements: Unit tests for policy, rehash, and the administrator passkey requirement

context.user_story: As a member whose device cannot make a passkey, I still want to be able to sign in.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
